entries.text: benchbox compare now exits 3 when a regression exceeds --fail-on-regression and 4 when the results cannot be compared, in both result-file mode and platform-run mode; exit 1 is left for errors such as a missing or unreadable result file.
details: Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error, 3 regression over threshold, 4 not comparable (different variants or timing modes). Codes 75 to 79 belong to the heavy-work host lock.
A script that treated exit 1 as 'regression' must now test for 3, and may treat 4 as 'inputs not comparable'. A pipeline step that fails on any non-zero status is unaffected.
A missing result file is now reported as exit 1 by compare itself rather than as a usage error.

entries.text: benchbox results validate checks one result file or a directory of them for integrity, completeness and believability, prints PASS, INFO, WARN and FAIL findings, offers --json and --fail-on-warn, and exits 5 when a file has a FAIL finding.
details: The findings are the ones the MCP validate_results tool returns for the same input; the repository script _project/scripts/validate_results.py now runs this command.

Directory validation skips submission manifests (*.manifest.json) as well as the other companion files, so a bundle directory is no longer reported with spurious FAILs; the MCP validate_results directory summary changes the same way.
